source.snippet: A just a single day of labor would pay for a fuel pump and line so nobody has to carry fuel drums up a staircase. If they expect 100% uptime they should be ready for something as common as a storm flood without risking injuries hauling fuel drums by hand. (Jane Street datacenter incident, 2026-11-11)

problem_statement: Small and mid-sized datacenter operators and colocation tenants lack affordable, automated disaster-readiness auditing tools that surface single points of failure in physical infrastructure (fuel supply chains, cooling redundancy, flood mitigation) before an incident exposes them.
target_segment: Datacenter operations managers and IT infrastructure leads at SMB colos or on-premise server rooms managing 99.9%+ uptime SLAs.
notes: The Jane Street anecdote illustrates that even sophisticated operators overlook cheap physical redundancy fixes. A paid checklist-and-audit SaaS (or one-time professional assessment service) targeting colo operators who pay for uptime insurance could find buyers. Willingness-to-pay evidence: commenter explicitly notes 'a single day of labor' cost justification, implying budget exists but process/tooling is absent.
